Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu Bilal Al-Ash'ari told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ja'far bin Abi Talib, some of the people of knowledge told me that when Abu Musa conquered Isfahan, he found one of the walls of the city had fallen, so he built it, but it fell, then he built it, but it fell, and he was told: There is a righteous man under it, so he dug the foundation and found a man standing with a sword on which was written: I am Al-Harith bin Mudadh, I took revenge on the people of the trench, so Abu Musa extracted it and rebuilt the wall, and it stood firm. I said: He is Al-Harith bin Mudadh bin Amr bin Mudadh bin Amr Al-Jurhumi, one of the kings of Jurhum who were in charge of the Kaaba after the son of Thabit bin Ismail bin Ibrahim, and the son of this Al-Harith is Amr bin Al-Harith bin Mudadh, he was the last king of Jurhum in Mecca when Khuza'a expelled them and exiled them to Yemen, and he is the one who said in his poem, which Ibn Hisham said was the first poem recited by the Arabs: As if there was no companion between Al-Hujun and Al-Safa, and no one spent the evening in Mecca Yes, we were its people, but the vicissitudes of night and misfortune destroyed us. This implies that this story took place long ago, after the time of Ishmael, peace be upon him, by nearly five hundred years or so. What Ibn Ishaq mentioned implies that their story took place during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both, which is more likely, and God knows best. It is possible that this happened many times in the world, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr, who said: The trench was in Yemen during the time of Tubba’ and in Constantinople during the time of Constantine when the Christians turned their qiblah away from the religion of Christ and monotheism, so they made a furnace and threw into it the Christians who followed the religion of Christ and monotheism. In Iraq, in the land of Babylon, there was Nebuchadnezzar, who made the idol and ordered the people to prostrate to it, but Daniel and his two companions, Azariah and Michael, refused, so he lit a furnace for them and threw wood and fire into it, then threw them into it. God made it cool and safe for them and saved them from it, but threw into it those who had transgressed against him, and they were nine men, and the fire consumed them. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the Almighty’s statement: The companions of the trench were killed. He said: The trench was three: a trench in Iraq, a trench in Syria, and a trench in Yemen. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and on the authority of Muqatil, he said: The trench was three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia. They were burned with fire. The one in Syria was Antoninus the Roman, the one in Persia was Bukhtanasr, and the one in the land of the Arabs was Yusuf Dhu Nuwas. As for the one in Persia and Syria, God Almighty did not send down a Qur’an regarding them, but He sent down the one in Najran. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, who is Ibn Anas, regarding the words of God Almighty: The companions of the trench were killed, he said: We heard that they were a people in a time of stagnation, and when they saw the tribulation and evil that had befallen the people and they became parties, each party rejoicing in what they had, they withdrew to a village and settled there and continued to worship God, devoting their religion to Him, being upright, and they established prayer and gave zakat. This was their situation until a tyrant heard about them and it happened. Their conversation, so he sent to them and ordered them to worship the idols they had taken, but they all refused him and said, We do not worship except God alone, with no partner for Him. So he said to them, If you do not worship these gods that I have worshipped, then I will fight you. But they refused him, so he made a trench of fire and the tyrant said to them and made them stand by it, Choose this or the one we are in. They said, This is more beloved to us. And among them were women and children. So the children were terrified and said to them, O my fathers, there is no fire after today. So they fell into it and their souls were taken before its heat touched them and the fire came out from its place and surrounded the tyrants, so God burned them with it. Concerning that, God, the Almighty, revealed: “The companions of the trench were destroyed. * The fire fueled * When they were sitting by it * And they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. * They did not blame them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy * To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And God is, over all things, Witness.” Ibn Jarir narrated it: I was told by Ammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Ja`far, with a similar narration. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who have persecuted the believing men and believing women meaning burned, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Abi Zayd, and then have not repented meaning they have not desisted from what they did and regretted what they did in the past, for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire. This is because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Look at this generosity and benevolence. They killed His friends while He was calling them to repentance and forgiveness.
85:10: God swears by the heaven and its constellations, which are the great stars, as was previously explained in His statement: Blessed is He who has placed in the heaven constellations and placed therein a lamp and a moon giving light. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and As-Suddi said: The constellations are the stars. Mujahid also said: The constellations in which are the guards. Yahya ibn Rafi’ said: The constellations are palaces in the heaven. Al-Minhal ibn Amr said: And the heaven with the constellations means beautiful creation. Ibn Jarir preferred that they are the mansions of the sun and the moon, which are twelve constellations. The sun travels through each of them for a month and the moon travels through each of them for two and a third days, so that is twenty-eight mansions and it lasts for two nights. And the Almighty said: And the Promised Day * And a witness and witnessed. The commentators differed on that. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Amr al-Ghazi told us, Ubaydullah - meaning Ibn Musa - told us, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid bin Safwan bin Aws al-Ansari, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And the Promised Day is the Day of Resurrection. And a witness is Friday. The sun does not rise or set on a day better than Friday. In it is an hour in which no Muslim servant asks God for good except that He gives it to him, and he does not seek refuge in Him from evil except that He protects him. And witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Khuzaymah narrated this hadith in this way through various chains of transmission on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah al-Rabdhi, whose hadith is weak. It was narrated as being attributed to Abu Hurayrah, which is more likely. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad told us, Shu’bah told us, I heard Ali bin Zaid and Yunus bin Ubaid narrating on the authority of Ammar, the freed slave of Banu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. As for Ali, he traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for Yunus, he did not mention Abu Hurayrah that he said about this verse, And a witness and what is witnessed. He said, He means the witness on Friday, and the witnessed day is the Day of Resurrection. Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Yunus, I heard Ammar, the freed slave of Banu Hashim narrating on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said about this verse, And a witness and what is witnessed. He said, The witness is on Friday, and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and what is promised is the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the same, and I have not seen them differ on that, praise be to God. Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf told us, Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, my father told us, Damdam ibn Zur’ah told us, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, and the witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah, and God has saved Friday for us. Then Ibn Jarir said: Sahl bin Musa al-Razi told us, Ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Ibn Harmalah, on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, that he said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The master of days is Friday, and it is the witness and the witnessed, the Day of Arafah. This is a mursal from the mursals of Saeed bin al-Musayyab. Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The witness is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: That is the Day when mankind will be gathered together, and that is the Day witnessed. Ibn Humayd told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Shubak, who said: A man asked al-Hasan bin Ali about the witness and the witnessed. He said: Did you ask anyone before me? He said: Yes, I asked Ibn Omar and Ibn Al-Zubayr and they said: The day of sacrifice and Friday. He said: No, but the witness is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he recited: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? And the witness is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: That is a Day when the people will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. And this is what Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, and Sufyan Al-Thawri said on the authority of Ibn Harmalah on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: And the one witnessed on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Al-Dahhak said: The witness is the son of Adam, and the one witnessed on the Day of Resurrection. And also on the authority of Ikrimah: The witness is Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the one witnessed is Friday. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The witness is God, and the one witnessed is on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Nu’aim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu Yahya Al-Qattat on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the witness and the one witnessed. He said: The witness is man, and the one witnessed is on Friday. This is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and a witness and what is witnessed: the witness is the Day of Arafah and what is witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. And it was narrated by Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Arafah means the witness and what is witnessed. Ibn Jarir said: And others said: The witnessed is Friday. And they narrated in that regard what Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman told us: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb told me, Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Zaid ibn Ayman, on the authority of Ubadah ibn Nassi, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Increase your prayers for me on Friday, for it is a witnessed day in which the angels witness. And on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr: The witness is God, and he recited: And sufficient is God as a witness, and what is witnessed is us. Al-Baghawi narrated it. And the majority said that the witness is Friday and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah. God the Almighty said: He cursed the companions of the ditch meaning He cursed the companions of the ditch, the plural of which is akhādīd, which is holes in the ground. This is report about a group of disbelievers who went to those who believed in God the Almighty and subdued them, wanting them to renounce their religion, but they refused. So they dug a ditch in the ground and lit a fire in it, preparing fuel to fuel it. Then they wanted to retaliate but they refused, so they threw them into it. For this reason God the Almighty said: He cursed the companions of the ditch * The fire fueled * When they were sitting by it * And they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. God the Almighty said: And they did not find fault with them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. Meaning, they had no sin against them except their belief in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, who does not wrong those who seek refuge in His impregnable side, in all of His words, deeds, laws, and decrees. Even if He had decreed for these servants what befell them at the hands of the disbelievers, then He is the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, even if the reason for that is hidden from many people. Then God the Almighty said: To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. The completion of the description is that He is the Owner of all the heavens and the earth and everything in them and between them. And God is Witness over all things. That is, nothing in the heavens or the earth is hidden from Him, and nothing is hidden from Him. The people of interpretation differed about who the people of this story were. According to Ali, they were the people of Persia when their king wanted to permit incest, but their scholars refused them, so he dug a trench and threw into it those who objected to him, and the practice of permitting incest has continued among them to this day. It was narrated from him that they were a people in Yemen whose believers and polytheists fought, and the believers defeated the disbelievers, then they fought and the disbelievers defeated the believers, so they dug trenches for them and burned them in them. It was narrated from him that they were from the people of Abyssinia, and one of them was an Abyssinian. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The companions of the trench were killed, the fire with fuel. He said: People from the Children of Israel dug a trench in the ground, then they lit a fire in it, then they placed men and women by that trench and paraded them over it, and they claimed that it was Daniel and his companions. This is what Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said, and other things were said. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Suhaib, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among those who came before you, there was a king who had a magician. When the magician grew old, he said to the king, ‘I have grown old and my time has come, so give me a boy so that I may teach him magic.’ So he gave him a boy, and he taught him magic. There was a monk between the magic and the king, so the boy went to the monk and listened to his speech, and he liked his manner and speech. When he went to the magician, he would hit him and say, ‘What held you back?’ And when he went to his family, they would hit him and say, ‘What held you back?’ So he complained about that to the monk, and he said, ‘If the magician wants to hit you, say, ‘My family held me back.’ And if your family wants to hit you, say, ‘The magician held me back.’ One day, while he was there, he came upon a huge, terrifying beast that had held people back so that they could not cross. So he said, ‘Today I know whether the matter of the monk is more beloved to God than the matter of magic.’ So he took a stone and said, ‘O God, if the matter of the monk is more beloved to You and more pleasing to You than the matter of the magician, then kill this beast.’” Until the people passed, and he threw it and killed it and the people went and the monk was told about that and he said, My son, you are better than me and you will be tested, so if you are tested do not point me out. So the boy cured the blind and the leper and all other diseases and healed them. The king had a companion who went blind and heard about him so he came to him with many gifts and said, Heal me and you will have what is here collected. He said, “I do not heal anyone, only God Almighty heals. If you believe in Him, I will call upon God and He will heal you.” So he believed and called upon God and He healed him. Then the king came and sat down in the same position as he had been sitting before. The king said to him, O so-and-so, who restored your sight? He said, My Lord. He said, No, my Lord and your Lord is God. He said, Do you have a lord other than me? He said, Yes, my Lord and your Lord is God. He continued torturing him until he directed him to the boy. Then the king sent for him and said, O my son, has your magic reached such an extent that you heal the blind, the leper, and these diseases? He said, I do not heal anyone; only God, the Almighty, the Majestic, heals. He said, Me? He said, No. He said, Do you have a lord other than me? He said, My Lord and your Lord is God. Then the king seized him again and continued torturing him until he directed him to the monk. Then the monk was brought and the king said, Return from your religion, but he refused. So the king placed the saw in the parting of his head until his sides fell off. He also said to the blind man, Return from your religion, but he refused. So the king placed the saw in the parting of his head until his sides fell off. The king said to the boy, Abandon your religion. He refused, so he sent him with some people to such-and-such a mountain and said, When you reach its peak, if he renounces his religion, well and good, roll him down from its top. So they took him, and when they had ascended the mountain, he said, O God, protect me from them however You wish. So the mountain shook and they were all rolled down. The boy came groping around until he entered upon the king. The king asked, What happened to your companions? He said, God has protected me from them. So he sent him with some people in a boat. He said, When you take him to the sea, if he renounces his religion, well and good, drown him in the sea. So they took him to the sea and the boy said, O God, protect me from them however You wish. So they were all drowned. The boy came until he entered upon the king. He said, What happened to your companions? He said, God sufficed me against them. Then he said to the king, "You will not kill me until you do what I command you. If you do what I command you, you will kill me. Otherwise, you will not be able to kill me." The king said, What is that? He said, "Gather the people in one plain, then crucify me on a tree-trunk and take an arrow from my quiver. Then say, 'In the name of God, Lord of the boy,' for if you do that, you will kill me." So he did and put the arrow to the bow of his bow and shot it, saying, In the name of God, Lord of the boy. The arrow struck his temple. The boy put his hand over the spot of the arrow and died. The people said, We believe in the Lord of the boy. The king was asked, Have you seen what you were fearing? By God, he has come to you and all people have believed. So he ordered that ditches be dug in the mouths of the streets and fires be set in them. He said: Whoever abandons his religion, let him go, otherwise throw him into it. He said: So they were competing in it and pushing each other. Then a woman came with her son to breastfeed, and it was as if she was reluctant to fall into the fire. The boy said: Be patient, O mother, for you are on the truth. And thus Muslim narrated it at the end of Sahih on the authority of Hadbah bin Khalid on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah with a similar chain of transmission. And al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Salman on the authority of Affan on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah and through the chain of transmission of Hammad bin Zaid, both of them on the authority of Thabit with it, and they shortened the beginning of it. And Imam Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi authenticated it as good, for he narrated it in the interpretation of this surah on the authority of Mahmud bin Ghailan and ‘Abd bin Hamid - the meaning is the same - they said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us on the authority of Mu’ammar on the authority of Thabit al-Banani on the authority of ‘Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Layla on the authority of Suhaib who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) prayed the ‘Asr prayer, he would whisper. And whispering in some of their sayings is moving the lips as if he is speaking. So it was said to him, ‘O Messenger of God, when you pray the ‘Asr prayer, you whisper.’ He said: ‘A prophet among the prophets was amazed by his nation and said: Who will stand up for these people?’ So God revealed to him that he gave them the choice between me taking revenge on them and me unleashing their enemy upon them, so they chose revenge, so God unleashed death upon them, and seventy thousand of them died in one day.’ He said: And whenever he narrated this hadith, he narrated this other hadith. He said: There was a king who had a priest who used to divine for him. The priest said: “Find me a young man who is intelligent, or he said: One who is perceptive and knowledgeable, so I can teach him this knowledge of mine.” So he mentioned the whole story, and at the end of it he said: God Almighty says: “Those who were with the trench were the fire fueled, when they were sitting by it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. They did not find fault with them except because they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.” He said: As for the boy, he was buried. It is mentioned that he was taken out during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, and his finger was on his temple as he had placed it when he was killed. Then al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and strange. This context does not explicitly state that the context of this story is from the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Our Sheikh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi said: It is possible that it is from the words of Suhayb al-Rumi, for he had knowledge of the report of the Christians, and God knows best. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned this story in the biography in another context in which it contradicts what was mentioned above. He said: Yazid ibn Ziyad told me on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, and some of the people of Najran also told me on the authority of its people that the people of Najran were polytheists who worshipped idols. There was in one of its villages near Najran - and Najran is the largest village to which the people of that country gathered - a magician who taught the boys of Najran magic. When he settled there, they did not name him to me by the name that Ibn Munabbih named him. They said: A man settled there and built a tent between Najran and that village where the magician was, and the people of Najran began to send their boys to that magician to teach them magic. Then Al-Tamir sent his son Abdullah bin Al-Tamir with the young men of Najran. Whenever he passed by the owner of the tent, he was pleased with what he saw of his worship and prayer, so he would sit next to him and listen to him until he converted to Islam and believed in the Oneness of God and worshipped Him. He would ask him about the laws of Islam until he understood it and began to ask him about the Greatest Name. He had taught it to him but he concealed it from him and said to him: O my nephew, you will not be able to bear it. I fear that you will be weak in it. Al-Tamir Abu Abdullah thought that his son would go to the magician as young men go. When Abdullah saw that his companion was stingy with him and feared that he would be weak in it, he took cups and gathered them. Then he did not leave any name of God that he knew without writing it in a cup, for each name a cup. When he had counted them, he lit a fire and began to throw cups into it. When he passed by the Greatest Name, he threw his cup into it. The cup jumped until it came out of it without harming it. He took it and brought it to his companion and told him that he had learned the Greatest Name that he had written. The companion said: What is it? He said: It is such and such. He said: How did you know that? So he told him what he had done. He said: O my nephew, you have harmed him, so hold back. I do not think you will do that. So whenever Abdullah bin Al-Tamir entered Najran, he would not encounter anyone suffering from any harm except that he would say to him: O Abdullah, will you declare God’s oneness and enter into my religion, and will I pray to God for you to be cured of the affliction you are suffering from? He said, Yes. So he declared God’s oneness and submitted, and he prayed to God for him, and he was cured until there remained no one in Najran who was afflicted with any harm except that he came to him. So he followed his command and prayed for him, and he was cured until his matter was brought to the king of Najran, who summoned him and said to him, You have corrupted the people of my village and opposed my religion and the religion of my fathers, so I will mutilate you. He said, You are not able to do that. He said, “So he began to send him to the high mountain and throw him on his head, and he fell to the ground with no harm in him. And he began to send him to the waters of Najran, seas in which nothing is thrown but perishes, and he was thrown into them, and he came out with no harm in him. When he defeated him, Abdullah bin al-Tamir said to him, “By God, you will not be able to kill me until you believe in what I believe in and declare God’s oneness, for if you do, you will have power over me and kill me.” So that king declared God’s oneness and bore witness to the testimony of Abdullah bin al-Tamir, then he struck him with a stick in his hand and wounded him with a small wound, so he killed him. The king perished on the spot, and the people of Najran gathered around the religion of Abdullah bin al-Tamir, and he remained as he had come. Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, from the Gospel and his rule, then what happened to the people of their religion happened to them, so from there the origin of the Christian religion was in Najran. Ibn Ishaq said: This is the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi and some of the people of Najran on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Tamir, and God knows best which one it was. He said: So Dhu Nuwas marched towards them with his army and called them to Judaism and gave them the choice between that or death, and they chose death. So he dug the trench and burned it with fire and killed with the sword, and mutilated them until he killed nearly twenty thousand of them. So it was about Dhu Nuwas and his army that God Almighty revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The companions of the trench were destroyed. The fire fueled, when they were sitting by it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. And they did not find fault with them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And God is, over all things, Witness.” This is how Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in the biography that the one who killed the companions of the trench was Dhu Nuwas, whose name was Zur`ah, and he was called Yusuf during his reign. He was the son of Bayan As`ad Abu Kurayb, who was Tubba’ who invaded Medina and covered the Ka`bah, and he took with him two rabbis from the Jews of Medina. So, some of the people of Yemen converted to Judaism at their hands, as Ibn In a single morning, Dhu Nuwas killed twenty thousand in the trench, and only one man, called Dos Dhu Tha’laban, escaped. He went as a horseman, and they pursued him but could not catch him. He went to Caesar, the king of Syria, who wrote to the Negus, the king of Abyssinia. He sent with him an army of Abyssinian Christians, led by Aryat and Abraha, and they rescued Yemen from the hands of the Jews. Dhu Nuwas fled, but he crossed the sea and drowned. The kingdom of Abyssinia remained in the hands of the Christians for seventy years. Then Saif bin Dhi Yazan Al-Himyari rescued him from the hands of the Christians when he sought help from Khosrau, the king of Persia. He sent with him those in the prisons, and they were close to seven hundred. He conquered Yemen with them, and the kingdom returned to Himyar. We will mention some of that, God willing, in the interpretation of Surah Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? Ibn Ishaq said: Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm told me that a man from Najran, during the time of Umar bin Al-Khattab, dug up a ruined area of Najran for some need. He found Abdullah bin Al-Tamir sitting under a burial place with his hand on a wound on his head, holding it with his hand. When he took his hand away from it, blood gushed out, and when he released his hand, it returned to it and held back its blood. On his hand was a ring on which was written, My Lord is God. He wrote to Umar bin Al-Khattab about it, informing him of his situation. Umar wrote to them to leave him as he was and to return him to the burial place he had been in, and they did so. Abu Bakr Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Al-Dunya, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu Bilal Al-Ash'ari told us, Ibrahim bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ja'far bin Abi Talib, some of the people of knowledge told me that when Abu Musa conquered Isfahan, he found one of the walls of the city had fallen, so he built it, but it fell, then he built it, but it fell, and he was told: There is a righteous man under it, so he dug the foundation and found a man standing with a sword on which was written: I am Al-Harith bin Mudadh, I took revenge on the people of the trench, so Abu Musa extracted it and rebuilt the wall, and it stood firm. I said: He is Al-Harith bin Mudadh bin Amr bin Mudadh bin Amr Al-Jurhumi, one of the kings of Jurhum who were in charge of the Kaaba after the son of Thabit bin Ismail bin Ibrahim, and the son of this Al-Harith is Amr bin Al-Harith bin Mudadh, he was the last king of Jurhum in Mecca when Khuza'a expelled them and exiled them to Yemen, and he is the one who said in his poem, which Ibn Hisham said was the first poem recited by the Arabs: As if there was no companion between Al-Hujun and Al-Safa, and no one spent the evening in Mecca Yes, we were its people, but the vicissitudes of night and misfortune destroyed us. This implies that this story took place long ago, after the time of Ishmael, peace be upon him, by nearly five hundred years or so. What Ibn Ishaq mentioned implies that their story took place during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both, which is more likely, and God knows best. It is possible that this happened many times in the world, as Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Al-Yaman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Jubayr, who said: The trench was in Yemen during the time of Tubba’ and in Constantinople during the time of Constantine when the Christians turned their qiblah away from the religion of Christ and monotheism, so they made a furnace and threw into it the Christians who followed the religion of Christ and monotheism. In Iraq, in the land of Babylon, there was Nebuchadnezzar, who made the idol and ordered the people to prostrate to it, but Daniel and his two companions, Azariah and Michael, refused, so he lit a furnace for them and threw wood and fire into it, then threw them into it. God made it cool and safe for them and saved them from it, but threw into it those who had transgressed against him, and they were nine men, and the fire consumed them. Asbat said on the authority of Al-Suddi regarding the Almighty’s statement: The companions of the trench were killed. He said: The trench was three: a trench in Iraq, a trench in Syria, and a trench in Yemen. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, and on the authority of Muqatil, he said: The trench was three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia. They were burned with fire. The one in Syria was Antoninus the Roman, the one in Persia was Bukhtanasr, and the one in the land of the Arabs was Yusuf Dhu Nuwas. As for the one in Persia and Syria, God Almighty did not send down a Qur’an regarding them, but He sent down the one in Najran. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki told us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja’far told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Rabi’, who is Ibn Anas, regarding the words of God Almighty: The companions of the trench were killed, he said: We heard that they were a people in a time of stagnation, and when they saw the tribulation and evil that had befallen the people and they became parties, each party rejoicing in what they had, they withdrew to a village and settled there and continued to worship God, devoting their religion to Him, being upright, and they established prayer and gave zakat. This was their situation until a tyrant heard about them and it happened. Their conversation, so he sent to them and ordered them to worship the idols they had taken, but they all refused him and said, We do not worship except God alone, with no partner for Him. So he said to them, If you do not worship these gods that I have worshipped, then I will fight you. But they refused him, so he made a trench of fire and the tyrant said to them and made them stand by it, Choose this or the one we are in. They said, This is more beloved to us. Its pen is light and its writing is light. God has three hundred and sixty moments in it every day. He creates and provides, causes death and brings to life, exalts and humiliates, and does what He wills.” End of the interpretation of Surat al-Buruj. Praise and thanks be to God.
85:22: God Almighty tells us about His believing servants that for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, unlike what He has prepared for His enemies of fire and Hell. That is why He said: That is the great attainment. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe, meaning that His punishment and vengeance against His enemies who denied His messengers and disobeyed His command is severe, mighty, and strong. He is the Almighty, the Possessor of mighty strength, who whatever He wills happens as He wills in the blink of an eye or even faster. That is why God Almighty said: Indeed, it is He who originates and restores, meaning from His perfect power and ability He originates creation and restores it as He began it, without any obstacle or resistance. And He is the Forgiving, the Loving, meaning He forgives the sin of whoever repents to Him and submits to Him, even if the sin was for anything. Ibn Abbas and others said: He is the Beloved. Possessor of the Throne, meaning the Owner of the Mighty Throne, high above all creation. Al-Majid has two readings: nominative, as an attribute of the Lord Almighty, and genitive, as an attribute of the Throne. Both have a correct meaning. He does what He wills, meaning whatever He wills. His actions are beyond question, and He is not questioned about what He does due to His greatness, power, wisdom, and justice. As we have narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, when he was on his deathbed, it was said to him: Did the doctor see you? He said: Yes. They said: What did he say to you? He said: He told me that I can do what I want. God the Almighty says: {Has there come to you the report of the hosts * Pharaoh and Thamud?} meaning, have you heard what God brought upon them of might and sent down upon them of punishment that no one could avert from them? This is a confirmation of God the Almighty’s saying: {Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe.} meaning, when He seizes the wrongdoer, He seizes him with a painful and severe seizure, the seizure of the Almighty, the Powerful. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by a woman who was reciting {Has there come to you the report of the hosts?} So he stood up to listen and said: Yes, it has come to me. God the Almighty says: {Rather, those who disbelieve are in denial} meaning, they are in doubt, suspicion, disbelief and stubbornness. {And God is behind them encompassing} meaning, He is Able to overcome them and they do not escape Him nor are they able to defeat Him. {Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an} meaning, great and noble. {In a Preserved Tablet} meaning, it is in the highest assembly, preserved from additions, omissions, distortions and alterations. Ibn Jarir said: Amr bin Ali told us, Qara bin Sulaiman told us, Harb bin Surayj told us, Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib told us on the authority of Anas bin Malik regarding the Almighty’s statement: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an * in a Preserved Tablet, he said: The Preserved Tablet that God mentioned, Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an * in a Preserved Tablet, is on the forehead of Israfil. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah bin Saleh told us that Abu Al-A’bas - he is Abd Al-Rahman bin Salman - said: There is nothing that God has decreed: the Qur’an, and what comes before it and what comes after it, except that it is in the Preserved Tablet. The Preserved Tablet is between the eyes of Israfil, and he is not permitted to look at it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: This glorious Qur’an is with God in a Preserved Tablet. He sends down from it whatever He wills to whomever He wills of His creation. Al-Baghawi narrated on the authority of Ishaq bin Bishr: Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj told me on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: At the beginning of the Tablet is: There is no god but God alone, His religion is Islam, and Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. So whoever believes in God, believes in His promise, and follows His Messengers, He will admit him into Paradise. He said: The Tablet is a tablet of white pearl, its length is the distance between the heaven and the earth, and its width is the distance between the east and the west. Its edges are of pearls and rubies, its covers are red rubies, its pen is light, its speech is bound to the Throne, and its root is in the lap of an angel. Muqatil said: The Preserved Tablet is to the right of the Throne. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Munjab ibn al-Harith told us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf told us, Ziyad ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Most High, created a Preserved Tablet of white pearl, its pages of red ruby. Its pen is light and its writing is light. God has three hundred and sixty moments in it every day. He creates and provides, causes death and brings to life, exalts and humiliates, and does what He wills.” End of the interpretation of Surat al-Buruj. Praise and thanks be to God.
